Hey Product Hunt!

Most programmatic video tools today rely on headless Chromium, Puppeteer, or canvas hacks. They are heavy, prone to frame drops, and hard for autonomous AI agents to drive reliably.

We built Framefields to rethink video creation from the ground up: a code-first video engine running on native WebGPU (Dawn, Metal, Vulkan) directly in Node.js—with zero browser overhead.

It combines what usually takes three desktop creative suites into one lightweight npm package:

• Motion Graphics & Typography: Kinetic text, SVG paths, Yoga layout trees, and spring/bezier curves. [...] • 2D Compositing & VFX: Photoshop-grade shaders (curves, film grain, LUTs, 3D relighting, chromatic aberration).

• Audio DSP & Sync: Sample-accurate beat grids, procedural SFX, EQ, and master compression.

• Built for AI Coding Agents: Deterministic frame clocks, visual frame-grid inspection, and hardware-accelerated MP4 export.

Everything is driven by TypeScript. Your agent or script writes code, verifies frames headlessly, and exports studio-grade video.

Check out our docs and open-source examples, and let us know what you think! What would you like to see next?

results.title: Locally Meshable Frame Fields
results.content: Frame Field Meshability. The most problematic robustness issue stems from a topological mismatch between frame felds and integer-grid maps, as described in [Pietroni et al. 2022; Reberol et al. 2019; Viertel et al. 2016]. In frame felds, additional topological structures exist, which do not correspond to any confguration available in a quad/hex mesh, and which make the generation of a locally injective integer-grid map impossible. The 2D setting, where singularities are isolated points in the domain, is already well-understood. The seminal work of Myles et al.  presents an algorithm that is capable of converting an input frame feld on a triangular mesh into a (globally) meshable one. Additional theoretical guarantees have been identifed in [Shen et al. 2022; Viertel and Osting 2019]. [...] Locally Meshable Frame Fields HENG LIU, University of Bern, Switzerland DAVID BOMMES, University of Bern, Switzerland input tet mesh with feature tags input frame feld input singularity graph output hex mesh [Beaufort et al. 2022] locally meshable frame feld locally meshable singularity graph output hex mesh (ours) Fig. 1. Overview. Non-meshable topological configurations in frame fields, e.g., invalid singularities or feature structures, induce degenerate integer-grid maps and broken and incomplete hex meshes (top row). Our algorithm (botom row) automatically turns a given frame field into a locally meshable one, where a valid integer-grid map enables a hex mesh that preserves all input features. [...] A typical integer-grid map approach consists of fve major steps sequentially generating (i) feature aligned frame feld, (ii) seamless map, (iii) integer quantization, (iv) integer-grid map, and (v) (poten-tially higher-order) hexahedral mesh. Provably robust algorithms exist only for the integer quantization (iii) [Brückler et al. 2022a] and the (linear) mesh extraction (v) [Lyon et al. 2016], while steps (i),(ii), and (iv) remain fragile.
